article_content: Stanford Medicine researchers have developed an innovative brain monitoring technique using temporary electrode implants in three epilepsy patients undergoing pre-surgical evaluation. The study identified specialized neurons in the intraparietal sulcus that activate exclusively during numerical calculations and quantitative thinking. Notably, these brain cells showed no activity during conversations, laughter, or memory recall. Researchers discovered unexpected activation patterns when patients heard number-related terms like 'many' or 'more than.' Published in Nature Communications, this real-time monitoring method provides new insights into everyday brain function. Dr. Josef Parvizi, lead researcher and director of Stanford's Human Intracranial Cognitive Electrophysiology Program (SHICEP), highlighted potential applications in developing communication devices for speech-impaired patients. While addressing science fiction concerns, Parvizi stressed current technology only detects numerical processing, not general thought decoding.

article_content: By Becky Barrow, Business Correspondent | Updated: 19 August 2013 UK house prices surged by £20,210 between January-August 2013, sparking concerns that government housing initiatives might fuel a property bubble. Data from Rightmove shows average asking prices in England and Wales reached £249,199 - nearly ten times the average annual salary. London's housing affordability crisis intensified, with average prices hitting £501,067 in August 2013, a 10% year-on-year increase. Housing charity Shelter revealed only 106,820 new homes were completed between May 2012-June 2013, far below the 250,000 annual target. Controversial 'Help to Buy' schemes faced scrutiny: The Institute of Directors labeled the policy 'very dangerous,' while economists questioned its sustainability. Rightmove's Miles Shipside emphasized the urgent need for increased housing supply to stabilize prices.

article_content: Milwaukee authorities have apprehended a man following a domestic violence incident resulting in two fatalities, including his five-month-old daughter. The tragedy occurred Friday morning around 8:30am at a duplex near 39th Street and Clybourn. First responders discovered the infant deceased in her crib and a 39-year-old family friend fatally wounded at the scene. The child's 19-year-old mother and her 22-year-old partner sustained life-threatening injuries during the attack but successfully contacted emergency services. Police confirmed the suspect, identified as the infant's biological father and the mother's former partner, was found in the home's bathroom with superficial self-inflicted wounds. Chief Edward Flynn disclosed that while the couple had a history of unreported domestic disputes, this marked the first official police involvement. The incident contributes to Milwaukee's 13 recorded homicides this January, compared to one case during the same period in 2014. Mayor Tom Barrett joined law enforcement at the scene, expressing concern over the city's atypical surge in violent crimes.
